c2458e3d6e: Validation: How a Genoryn Krypton Full Node Protects Your GNR
8a1663d161: Do not take anyone's word for it.
a74f0174e2: A payment is worth what the rules behind it are worth, and the rules are only real for someone who checks them. A Genoryn Krypton full node checks every block it receives, in full, before it believes anything in it. It trusts no miner, no website and no other node.
9b8cf5dd54: Imagine being handed a banknote and being able to test, in two milliseconds, that it was printed by the rules and that there will never be more than 21 million of them. That is what a full node does with every GNR, including the ones nobody has paid you yet.
f127d2dbc0: Each block's KryptoHash proof of work, against a difficulty that the node computes itself from the 90 blocks before it. A block with too little work is not a block.
c488759067: Each transfer carries a zk-STARK proof that its inputs exist, belong to the spender and add up to its outputs and fee. The node verifies every one, in about 2 ms each. A transfer that creates GNR from nothing has no valid proof.
fcface9eb4: Spending a note reveals its nullifier. The node keeps every nullifier ever seen and refuses a block that repeats one.
0d07dfdc29: 5 GNR per block, halving every 2,100,000 blocks, 21,000,000 in all. The node adds the reward up itself; a block that pays out more is refused whatever work stands behind it.
e2af49c4c1: Mining rewards go to a pool and are paid by shares. The node checks every share's work and every payout against the accounts it keeps, so no miner can pay itself another's reward.
c4ebb36bb3: Timestamps, sizes, the note tree's root, the commitment to all earlier blocks. When two chains compete, the node follows the valid one with the most work, and no other.
a6194a9de5: There are three ways to hold GNR: let someone else hold it for you, use the light wallet, or run a full node. They stop different attacks.
c0160a7edc: <0>Direct theft.</0> The holder of your coins disappears, is hacked, or freezes your account.
017ecf2614: <0>A payment that does not exist.</0> You are shown an incoming payment and hand over goods; the payment was never real.
cfcdf82d91: <0>Exposed</0><1/>You see what their website shows you.
4fae8bf008: <0>Partly</0><1/>A payment counts only when it is in a block whose proof of work the wallet has checked, so faking one takes real mining work for every confirmation. The wallet does not re-verify the payment's own proof: wait for several confirmations for larger amounts.
47a4cb02ae: <0>Protected</0><1/>The node has verified the payment's own proof, also while it still waits for a block.
4b0e04057c: <0>Broken rules.</0> Miners with most of the hashrate mine blocks that create GNR from nothing or spend other people's coins.
97dd629031: <0>Partly</0><1/>It follows the chain with the most work above a checkpoint, and does not re-verify other people's proofs. A majority of the hashrate could show it such a chain.
8c0c5a95c2: <0>Protected</0><1/>An invalid block is refused however much work it carries. To a full node that chain does not exist.
b3930c0ebf: <0>A cheap fake chain.</0> A node shows you a private chain where you were paid.
5e6b33395e: <0>Protected</0><1/>The wallet samples the whole history, checks the work, remembers the most work it has seen and refuses less. Faking confirmations costs as much as honest mining.
8b462cb1b8: <0>Hiding a payment from you.</0> The node you ask leaves your incoming payment out.
3ff9049d46: <0>Partly</0><1/>A block's outputs are checked against its header, so nothing can be left out of a block unnoticed. A node can only stall; several nodes are cross-checked.
8aeffeefb8: <0>Protected</0><1/>It hears every block from many peers.
ab2fd301ca: <0>Being watched.</0> Whoever serves you learns what you own.
0b71b68d7f: <0>Partly</0><1/>A node sees your internet address and that you sync. It does not learn which notes are yours: the wallet downloads whole blocks and whole parts of the note tree.
80ae1ccc2c: <0>Rewriting history.</0> Someone with enough hashrate replaces recent blocks and takes a payment back.
555366cf2d: <0>Partly</0><1/>Nothing stops this but work. Every confirmation makes it cost more: wait for more of them for larger amounts.
89e456adf2: The last row is true of every proof-of-work currency, Bitcoin included. A full node cannot prevent a rewrite; it can only make sure that what replaces the old blocks obeys every rule too.
51fb779eae: Stronger than "simple payment verification", and honest about its limit
6c39fbe7ca: Most light wallets of other currencies ask a server and believe the answer. The Genoryn Krypton wallet does not. Every block header commits to all blocks before it and to the work in them, so the wallet can check, with a few hundred samples, that the chain it is shown is the one with the most work; it refuses blocks dated in the future, a chain without the release's checkpoint, and any chain lighter than one it has already seen. Then it checks every block it reads against that block's header.
59cc4c2aec: What it does not do is re-verify the proofs inside other people's transactions. For that it relies on the miners who built on the block, like every light wallet does. A full node relies on nobody.
477400d2e3: For everyday amounts the light wallet is a sound choice. If you accept large payments, run a business on GNR, or simply want to depend on no one, run a full node and point your wallet at it.
